question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and if so should it be a static artifact, an authenticated runtime endpoint, or a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema generation path?
rationale: The request would define a supported external Gateway API surface, including auth, endpoint visibility, plugin surfaces, versioning, and upgrade compatibility, so automation should not choose the contract shape.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Limit the first step to a committed or release-attached schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime schema endpoint.

options.title: Defer To Existing Protocol Schema
options.body: Decide that TypeBox plus generated JSON Schema and Gateway RPC docs are the intended client-generation surface, then close only after documenting that direction clearly.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway protocol/schema and HTTP routing history makes this the strongest current-main routing signal for the public API boundary decision.
